facts.statement: The genus Nemegtomaia was described by Lü and colleagues in 2005.
facts.quote: authority: Lü et al., 2005

facts.statement: The type species of the genus is Nemegtomaia barsboldi.
facts.quote: type_species: Nemegtomaia barsboldi

facts.statement: Nemegtomaia lived in what is now Mongolia during the Late Cretaceous, approximately 72 to 70 million years ago.
facts.quote: Nemegtomaia is a genus of oviraptorid dinosaur from what is now Mongolia that lived in the Late Cretaceous Period, about 72 to 70 million years ago.

facts.statement: The first specimen of Nemegtomaia was discovered in 1996 and formally named in 2004.
facts.quote: The first specimen was found in 1996, and became the basis of the new genus and species N. barsboldi in 2004.

facts.statement: The original genus name Nemegtia was replaced by Nemegtomaia in 2005 because the former name was already in use.
facts.quote: The original genus name was Nemegtia, but this was changed to Nemegtomaia in 2005, as the former name was preoccupied.

facts.statement: The name Nemegtomaia means "good mother of the Nemegt," referencing the genus's association with egg-brooding behavior.
facts.quote: The first part of the generic name refers to the Nemegt Basin, where the animal was found, and the second part means "good mother", in reference to the fact that oviraptorids are known to have brooded their eggs.

facts.statement: The species name barsboldi honors the paleontologist Rinchen Barsbold.
facts.quote: The specific name honours the palaeontologist Rinchen Barsbold.

facts.statement: Nemegtomaia was estimated to be about 2 meters (7 feet) long and weigh 40 kilograms (85 pounds).
facts.quote: Nemegtomaia is estimated to have been around 2 m (7 ft) in length, and to have weighed 40 kg (85 lb).

facts.statement: As an oviraptorosaur, Nemegtomaia would have been covered in feathers.
facts.quote: As an oviraptorosaur, it would have been feathered.

facts.statement: Nemegtomaia had a deep, narrow, short skull featuring an arched crest.
facts.quote: It had a deep, narrow, and short skull, with an arched crest.

facts.statement: Nemegtomaia had three fingers, with the first being the largest and bearing a strong claw.
facts.quote: It had three fingers; the first was largest and bore a strong claw.

facts.statement: The eggs associated with the nesting specimen were estimated to be 5 to 6 cm wide and 14 to 16 cm long when intact.
facts.quote: None of the eggs are complete, but they are estimated to have been 5 to 6 cm (2 to 2.3 in) wide and 14 to 16 cm (5 to 6 in) long when intact.

facts.statement: Evidence suggests Nemegtomaia preferred to nest near streams to access soft, sandy substrate and food.
facts.quote: The specimen was found in a stratigraphic area that indicates Nemegtomaia preferred nesting near streams that would provide soft, sandy substrate and food.

facts.statement: Damage on the nesting specimen's skeleton indicates it was scavenged by skin beetles.
facts.quote: The skeleton of the nesting specimen has damage that indicates it was scavenged by skin beetles.

facts.statement: The diet of oviraptorids is uncertain, though their skulls resemble those of known or suspected herbivores.
facts.quote: The diet of oviraptorids is uncertain, but their skulls are most similar to other animals that are known or thought to have been herbivorous.

facts.statement: Nemegtomaia fossils are found in the Nemegt and Baruungoyot formations, representing environments that included both humid and arid conditions.
facts.quote: Nemegtomaia is known from the Nemegt and Baruungoyot formations, which are thought to represent humid and arid environments that coexisted in the same area.

facts.statement: Yoshitsugu Kobayashi discovered an incomplete oviraptorid skeleton in the Nemegt Formation of the Gobi Desert in 1996.
facts.quote: In 1996 the palaeontologist Yoshitsugu Kobayashi (as part of the "Mongolian Highland International Dinosaur Project" team) found an incomplete skeleton of an oviraptorid dinosaur in the Nemegt Formation of the Gobi Desert in southwestern Mongolia.

facts.statement: In 2002, Lü Junchang and colleagues described the first specimen as an uncertain species of the genus Ingenia.
facts.quote: The specimen was described as a new specimen of the genus Ingenia (referred to as Ingenia sp.; of uncertain species) by the palaeontologist Lü Junchang and colleagues in 2002

facts.statement: In 2004, Lü and colleagues designated the specimen as the holotype for the new species Nemegtia barsboldi.
facts.quote: In 2004 Lü and colleagues determined that the skeleton belonged to a new, distinct taxon, and made it the holotype specimen of Nemegtia barsboldi.

facts.statement: In 2005, researchers realized the name Nemegtia was preoccupied by a genus of freshwater seed shrimp described in 1978.
facts.quote: In 2005 the describers discovered (after being notified by a biologist) that the name Nemegtia had already been used for a genus of freshwater seed shrimp (Ostracoda) from the same formation in 1978, and was therefore preoccupied.

facts.statement: Two new specimens of Nemegtomaia were discovered in 2007 and formally described in 2013.
facts.quote: In 2007 two new specimens of Nemegtomaia were found by the "Dinosaurs of the Gobi" expedition, and were described by the palaeontologist Federico Fanti and colleagues in 2013.

facts.statement: The second specimen was found by Nicholas R. Longrich in the Nemegt Formation and includes hands, partial limbs, ribs, and a partial pelvis.
facts.quote: The second specimen, MPC-D 107/16, was found by the palaeontologist Nicholas R. Longrich in the Nemegt Formation, and consists of the hands, a partial left ulna and radius, ribs, a partial pelvis, and both femora.

facts.statement: The first new specimen was found less than 500 meters from the holotype and was assigned to Nemegtomaia based on similar anatomy and location.
facts.quote: This specimen was found less than 500 m (1640 ft) from the holotype, and was of the same size; it was assigned to Nemegtomaia due to its similar anatomical features and geographical proximity.

facts.statement: While lacking unique single features, the combination of a crest, enlarged first finger, and eight sacral vertebrae is unique to Nemegtomaia.
facts.quote: Though Nemegtomaia does not possess any single feature that distinguishes it from other oviraptorids (autapomorphies), the combination of a crest, an enlarged first finger, and a high number of sacral vertebrae (eight), is unique to this taxon.

facts.statement: Nemegtomaia possessed a well-developed crest formed primarily by the premaxilla bones of its snout.
facts.quote: It had a well-developed crest, formed by the nasal and premaxilla bones (mainly the latter) of the snout.

facts.statement: The eye opening of Nemegtomaia measured 52 mm or 2 inches, making the eyes appear large relative to the short skull.
facts.quote: The diameter of the orbit (eye opening) was 52 mm (2 in); the eyes looked large due to the shortness of the skull.

facts.statement: Nemegtomaia had toothless jaws with a short snout featuring a deep, robust, parrot-like beak.
facts.quote: The jaws of Nemegtomaia were toothless, and like other oviraptorid dinosaurs, it had a short snout with a deep, robust, and somewhat parrot-like beak.

facts.statement: Small openings on the front of the snout likely served as nutrient channels and indicate the presence of a keratinous bill.
facts.quote: Nemegtomaia had small foramina (openings) on the sides of the suture (joint) between the premaxillae at the front of the snout, which may have been nutrient openings (and which indicate the presence of a keratinous bill).

facts.statement: The lower jaw of Nemegtomaia was short, deep, and convex, reaching 153 mm or 6 inches in length.
facts.quote: The lower jaw was short and deep, with a convex lower surface, and reached 153 mm (6 in) in length.

facts.statement: The shoulder blade of Nemegtomaia appears to have been 185 mm or 7 inches in total length.
facts.quote: The scapula (shoulder blade) appears to have been 185 mm (7 in) in total length.

facts.statement: The upper arm bone had a bird-like depression but was atypical for oviraptorosaurs, measuring 152 mm or 6 inches long.
facts.quote: The humerus (upper arm bone) had a fossa (depression) in a position similar to modern birds, but atypical among oviraptorosaurs, and appears to have been 152 mm (6 in) long.

facts.statement: The thigh bone was estimated to be 286 mm or 11 inches long, while the lower leg bone was 317 mm or 12 inches long.
facts.quote: The femur (thigh bone) is estimated to have been 286 mm (11 in) long, and the tibia of the lower leg 317 mm long (12 in).

facts.statement: In 2010, Longrich and colleagues classified Nemegtomaia in the family Oviraptoridae and subfamily Ingeniinae, noting it was the only member of that subfamily with a prominent crest.
facts.quote: In 2010 Longrich and colleagues determined that Nemegtomaia belonged in the family Oviraptoridae, as part of the subfamily Ingeniinae, making it the only member of the latter group with a prominent crest.

facts.statement: In 2012, Fanti and colleagues placed Nemegtomaia in Ingeniinae as a derived member closest to Heyuannia based on hand proportions.
facts.quote: In 2012 Fanti and colleagues also found Nemegtomaia to be part of Ingeniinae as a derived member, closest to Heyuannia, due to the proportions of the hands of the two new specimens (relatively short with a robust first finger).

facts.statement: The subfamily name Ingeniinae has been replaced by Heyuanninae because the name Ingenia was preoccupied.
facts.quote: The subfamily name Ingeniinae has since been replaced by the name Heyuanninae (since Ingenia was preoccupied).

facts.statement: The family Oviraptoridae, to which Nemegtomaia belongs, is exclusively known from the Upper Cretaceous of Asia, with most genera found in the Gobi Desert of Mongolia and China.
facts.quote: The family Oviraptoridae (to which Nemegtomaia belongs) consisted of generally small members, and is exclusively known from the Upper Cretaceous of Asia, with most genera having been discovered in the Gobi Desert of Mongolia and China.

facts.statement: Gregory S. Paul suggested in 2010 that crestless oviraptorids were juveniles or females of crested species, implying the number of genera in the group was exaggerated.
facts.quote: In 2010, the palaeontologist Gregory S. Paul suggested that crestless oviraptorids were either the juveniles or females of otherwise crested species, and that the number of genera in the group was therefore exaggerated.

facts.statement: Other researchers argue that dromaeosaurs and troodontids are most closely related to birds, placing oviraptorosaurs outside this group.
facts.quote: Other researchers have instead found dromaeosaurs and troodontids to be most closely related to birds, together forming the group Paraves; oviraptorosaurs, therizinosaurs, and alvarezsaurs are just outside this group.

facts.statement: A fossil of Nemegtomaia was discovered in a brooding posture over a nest containing eggs.
facts.quote: The Nemegtomaia specimen MPC-D 107/15 was found associated with a nest with eggs; its feet were placed in the centre of what was probably a ring of eggs, with the arms folded across the tops of the eggs on each side of the body

facts.statement: The fossilized nest associated with the Nemegtomaia specimen measures approximately 90 cm wide and 100 cm long.
facts.quote: The collected part of the nest is about 90 cm (35 in) wide and 100 cm (30 in) long

facts.statement: Seven distinct eggs and fragments were found within the nest, some located beneath the skeleton's skull and limbs.
facts.quote: Most eggs (seven distinct eggs have been identified) and egg fragments were recovered either in the lower layer of the nest or under the skull, neck, and limbs of the specimen

facts.statement: Eggs of the Oviraptoridae family, including those of Nemegtomaia, average about 17 cm in length.
facts.quote: Oviraptorid eggs appear to have been 17 cm (6 in) long on average

facts.statement: Researchers suggest the eggs in the Nemegtomaia nest were likely displaced by burial, wind, sandstorms, or predators.
facts.quote: The eggs of MPC-D 107/15 were therefore most likely displaced during burial, or by external factors, such as strong winds, sandstorms, or predators

facts.statement: No complete eggs or embryos were preserved in the nest, preventing full reconstruction of the clutch.
facts.quote: The nest does not preserve any complete eggs or embryos, which prevents determination of the size, shape, number, and arrangement of the eggs in the nest

facts.statement: Evidence suggests the original nest likely had two layers of eggs beneath the parent, with no eggs in the center.
facts.quote: It is probable that there were originally two layers of eggs below the body, and there do not appear to have been eggs in the centre of the nest

facts.statement: Nemegtomaia likely nested near streams in otherwise dry environments to access soft sand and food.
facts.quote: The nesting specimen was found in a stratigraphic area indicating that oviraptorids preferred nesting near streams that provided soft, sandy substrate and food in environments that were otherwise xeric

facts.statement: Brooding positions found in many oviraptorids suggest they may have incubated eggs for over 40 days with limited food.
facts.quote: Many oviraptorids have been found in brooding positions, indicating they may have brooded for relatively long periods, similar to modern birds such as the ostrich, emu, and black-breasted buzzard, which brood for more than 40 days with a limited supply of sustenance

facts.statement: Researchers suggest tail feathers in oviraptorosaurs evolved to shade and protect eggs in the nest.
facts.quote: It has also been suggested that the evolution of tail-feathers in oviraptorosaurs was an adaptation for shading and protecting eggs in their nests

facts.statement: The reduction of the second finger in heyuannine oviraptorids is hypothesized to be related to supporting long wing feathers used for egg protection.
facts.quote: That the second finger of heyuannine oviraptorids was reduced in size compared to the robust first finger may be explained by a change in function; it may be related to the presence of long wing feathers that were attached to the second finger

facts.statement: Researchers suggest cuticle layers on oviraptorid eggs were an adaptation for reproductive success in variable environments.
facts.quote: The researchers suggested that the cuticle-coated eggs would have been a trait adapted for enhancing their reproductive success in the variable environments where Nemegtomaia and other oviraptorids nested

facts.statement: Studies suggest multiple individuals may have gathered eggs in a single nest to be guarded by one individual, possibly a male.
facts.quote: Various studies have suggested that several individuals would gather eggs in a single nest, and arrange them so they could be protected by one individual, possibly a male

facts.statement: In 2010, David J. Varricchio and colleagues noted that oviraptorid clutch sizes resemble those of modern archosaurs with polygamous mating and extensive male parental care.
facts.quote: In 2010 the palaeontologist David J. Varricchio and colleagues found that the relatively large clutch-size of oviraptorids and troodontids is most similar to those of modern archosaurs (birds and crocodilians, the closest living relatives of dinosaurs) that practice polygamous mating and extensive male parental care

facts.statement: In 2013, W. Scott Persons and colleagues suggested that feather-fans on oviraptorosaur tails were used for intraspecific communication like courtship.
facts.quote: Many oviraptorosaurs are known to have had pygostyles on the end of their tails, which suggests the presence of feather-fans; the palaeontologist W. Scott Persons and colleagues suggested in 2013 that these could have been used for intraspecific communication such as courtship rituals

facts.statement: In 2026, Chun-Yu Su and colleagues conducted an experiment to test if oviraptorids used body heat for incubation.
facts.quote: The palaeontologist Chun-Yu Su and colleagues devised an experiment to evaluate whether oviraptorids employed thermoregulatory contact incubation to provide heat for embryonic development in 2026

facts.statement: Experiments showed that oviraptorid brooding would result in uneven temperatures and lower incubation efficiency compared to modern birds.
facts.quote: The results showed that the incubator only partially covered the eggs in the outer ring of the clutch, which led to a difference in temperature between the inner and outer eggs, and therefore lower incubation efficiency than in modern birds

facts.statement: Researchers concluded that oviraptorids likely co-regulated incubation using environmental and solar heat rather than body heat alone.
facts.quote: These researchers concluded that their experiment did not support thermoregulatory contact incubation in oviraptorids, instead suggesting they co-regulated their incubation with environmental heat (in conjunction with solar input)

facts.statement: Temperature differences in oviraptorid nests suggest they did not use temperature-dependent sex determination.
facts.quote: The large difference between incubation temperatures in the two oviraptorids suggests they did not have temperature-dependent sex determination (which is used by for example crocodiles), as the sex-ratios would be skewed

facts.statement: Research in 2010 suggested that the jaws of oviraptorids, including Nemegtomaia, shared structural similarities with herbivorous animals like dicynodonts.
facts.quote: In 2010 Longrich and colleagues found that oviraptorid jaws had features similar to those seen in herbivorous tetrapods (four-limbed animals), especially those of dicynodonts, an extinct group of synapsid stem-mammals.

facts.statement: In 2017, researchers proposed that the parrot-like jaws of oviraptorids might indicate a diet including fruits, nuts, and seeds.
facts.quote: In 2017, the palaeontologist Gregory F. Funston and colleagues suggested that the parrot-like jaws of oviraptorids may indicate a frugivorous diet that incorporated nuts and seeds.

facts.statement: It is hypothesized that oviraptorid jaws were adapted for processing dry vegetation, though this cannot be confirmed due to a lack of knowledge about the ancient flora.
facts.quote: The jaws of oviraptorids may have been specialised for processing food, such as xerophytic vegetation (adapted for environments with little water), that would have grown in their environment, but this is not possible to demonstrate, as little is known about the flora of the area at the time.

facts.statement: While the forelimbs of some oviraptorids resemble those of modern insect-eaters, their jaw morphology suggests they were not insectivorous.
facts.quote: Longrich and colleagues pointed out that the robust forelimbs and enlargement of a single finger in heyuannine oviraptorids is similar to that seen in modern animals that eat ants and termites, such as anteaters and pangolins, but the morphology of heyuannine jaws does not support them being insectivorous.

facts.statement: In 2004, researchers proposed that the skull bones of Nemegtomaia were movable, potentially affecting jaw function.
facts.quote: In 2004 Lü and colleagues proposed that the articulation between the quadrate and quadratojugal bones in the skull of Nemegtomaia suggested that these bones were movable in relation to each other, which would have affected how the jaws functioned.

facts.statement: A 2015 study found it unlikely that Nemegtomaia possessed bird-like skull mobility because the quadrate bone was immobile.
facts.quote: In 2015 the Belgian palaeontologist Christophe Hendrickx and colleagues found it unlikely that Nemegtomaia and other oviraptords had bird-like kinesis in their skulls, due to the quadrate bone being immobile.

facts.statement: Nemegtomaia lived approximately 70 million years ago during the Late Cretaceous period, specifically the upper Campanian to lower Maastrichtian ages.
facts.quote: Nemegtomaia is known from the Nemegt and Baruungoyot Formations, which date to the upper Campanian–lower Maastrichtian ages of the Late Cretaceous period, about 70 million years ago.

facts.statement: Nemegtomaia inhabited environments ranging from humid river systems to arid, wind-swept areas, as evidenced by the different rock formations where fossils were found.
facts.quote: The rock facies of the Nemegt Formation are thought to represent a humid, fluvial (associated with rivers and streams) environment, whereas those of the Baruungoyot Formation are thought to represent an arid or semi-arid environment, with aeolian (affected by wind) beds.

facts.statement: The habitat of the Nemegt Formation has been compared to the modern Okavango Delta in Botswana.
facts.quote: The environment of the Nemegt Formation has been compared to the Okavango Delta of present-day Botswana.

facts.statement: The rivers of the Nemegt Formation supported diverse aquatic life including molluscs, fish, turtles, and the crocodylomorph Shamosuchus.
facts.quote: The habitats in and around the Nemegt rivers provided a home for a wide array of organisms. Aquatic animals include molluscs, fish, turtles, and the crocodylomorph Shamosuchus.

facts.statement: The Nemegt Formation contained herbivorous dinosaurs such as the ankylosaurid Tarchia, the pachycephalosaur Prenocephale, hadrosaurs like Saurolophus, and sauropods like Nemegtosaurus.
facts.quote: Herbivorous dinosaurs of the Nemegt Formation include ankylosaurids such as Tarchia, the pachycephalosaurian Prenocephale, hadrosaurids such as Saurolophus and Barsboldia, and sauropods such as Nemegtosaurus, and Opisthocoelicaudia.

facts.statement: The Nemegt Formation also hosted various theropods including tyrannosauroids like Tarbosaurus, troodontids like Borogovia, therizinosaurs like Therizinosaurus, and ornithomimosaurians like Gallimimus.
facts.quote: Other theropods include tyrannosauroids such as Tarbosaurus, Alioramus, and Bagaraatan, troodontids such as Borogovia, Tochisaurus, and Saurornithoides, therizinosaurs such as Therizinosaurus, and ornithomimosaurians such as Deinocheirus, Anserimimus, and Gallimimus.

facts.statement: In 2016, researchers suggested that oviraptorids preferred drier environments while their relatives, caenagnathids, preferred riverine environments.
facts.quote: In 2016 the Japanese palaeontologist Takanobu Tsuihiji and colleagues suggested that oviraptorids may have preferred drier environments, while caenagnathids preferred fluvial environments, based on the type of formations they have been found in.

facts.statement: Research suggests that oviraptorids occupied both dry and wet environments but were more common in dry areas, potentially coexisting with other oviraptorosaurs through dietary niche partitioning.
facts.quote: Funston and colleagues suggested that oviraptorids were found in both xeric and mesic environments (but were more abundant in the former), whereas the other oviraptorosaur groups avoided the xeric environments, and that the coexistence of the families can be explained by niche partitioning in diet.

facts.statement: The fossil specimen of Nemegtomaia was preserved in sediment deposited by a sandstorm or dune shift.
facts.quote: The specimen is preserved in facies that are thought to have been deposited through a sandstorm or dune-shift.

facts.statement: Evidence of borings and burrows in the Nemegtomaia fossil indicates it was scavenged by colonies of skin beetles and possibly other insects.
facts.quote: Borings in the bones, burrows, and reworked sediments (perhaps caused by the construction of pupal chambers) in the specimen indicate it was scavenged upon by colonies of skin beetles (Dermestidae) and perhaps other scavenging insects.

facts.statement: Tunnels found in the nest area under the neck and skull of the Nemegtomaia specimen suggest insect activity, yet no eggs were found in those specific areas.
facts.quote: There are also tunnels in the nest under the neck and skull, and no egg remains have been found in parts with such traces.

facts.statement: The first specimen was found in 1996 and served as the basis for the new genus and species N. barsboldi in 2004.
facts.quote: El primer espécimen se encontró en 1996 y se convirtió en la base del nuevo género y especie N. barsboldi en 2004.

facts.statement: It lived during the late Cretaceous period, approximately 70 million years ago in the Maastrichtian, in what is now Asia.
facts.quote: que vivió a finales del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente 70 millones de años, en el Maastrichtiense, en lo que hoy es Asia.

facts.statement: Nemegtomaia is estimated to have been around 2 meters in length and weighed 40 kilograms.
facts.quote: Se estima que la Nemegtomaia medía alrededor de 2 metros de longitud y pesaba 40 kilogramos.

facts.statement: As an oviraptorosaurian, it would have been feathered.
facts.quote: Como un oviraptorosauriano, habría sido emplumado.

facts.statement: It had a deep, narrow, and short skull with an arched crest.
facts.quote: Tenía un cráneo profundo, estrecho y corto, con una cresta arqueada.

facts.statement: It had no teeth, a short snout with a beak similar to a parrot, and a pair of tooth-like projections on the palate.
facts.quote: No tenía dientes, tenía un hocico corto con un pico similar a un loro y un par de proyecciones similares a dientes en el paladar.

facts.statement: It had three fingers, with the first being larger and possessing a strong claw.
facts.quote: Tenía tres dedos, el primero era más grande y tenía una garra fuerte.

facts.statement: The skull was deep, narrow, and short compared to the rest of the body, reaching 179 millimeters in length.
facts.quote: El cráneo de Nemegtomaia era profundo, estrecho y corto, en comparación con el resto del cuerpo y alcanzaba 179 milímetros de longitud.

facts.statement: The eye orbit diameter was 52 millimeters, making the eyes appear large due to the small skull size.
facts.quote: El diámetro de la órbita ocular fue de 52 milímetros, los ojos se veían grandes debido a lo pequeño del cráneo.

facts.statement: The jaws had no teeth, and like other oviraptorid dinosaurs, it had a short snout with a deep, robust beak somewhat similar to a parrot.
facts.quote: Las mandíbulas de Nemegtomaia no tenían dientes, y al igual que otros dinosaurios oviraptóridos, tenía un hocico corto con un pico profundo, robusto y algo parecido a un loro.

facts.statement: The nesting specimen was positioned on top of what was likely a ring of eggs, with its arms crossed over them.
facts.quote: El espécimen de Nemegtomaia anidado se colocó encima de lo que probablemente era un anillo de huevos, con los brazos cruzados sobre ellos.

facts.statement: None of the eggs are complete, but they are estimated to be 5 to 6 centimeters wide and 14 to 16 centimeters long when intact.
facts.quote: Ninguno de los huevos está completo, pero se estima que tienen 5 a 6 centímetros de ancho y 14 a 16 centímetros de largo cuando están intactos.

facts.statement: The skeleton of the nesting specimen has damage indicating it was eaten by skin beetles.
facts.quote: El esqueleto del espécimen de anidación tiene daños que indican que fue comido por escarabajos de la piel.

facts.statement: Nemegtomaia may have protected its eggs by covering them with its tail and wing feathers.
facts.quote: Nemegtomaia puede haber protegido sus huevos cubriéndolos con sus plumas de cola y alas.

facts.statement: The scapula appears to have been 185 millimeters in total length.
facts.quote: La escápula parece haber sido de 185 milímetros de longitud total.

facts.statement: The humerus had a fossa in a position similar to modern birds but atypical among oviraptorosaurians, and appears to have measured 152 millimeters in length.
facts.quote: El húmero tenía una fosa en una posición similar a las aves modernas, pero atípica entre los oviraptorosaurianos, y parece haber medido 152 milímetros de largo.

facts.statement: The femur was 286 millimeters long and the tibia of the lower leg was 317 millimeters long.
facts.quote: El fémur tenía 286 milímetros de largo y la tibia de la parte inferior de la pierna 317 milímetros de largo.

facts.statement: The lower jaw was short and deep, with a convex lower surface, and reached 153 millimeters in length.
facts.quote: La mandíbula inferior era corta y profunda, con una superficie inferior convexa y alcanzaba 153 milímetros de longitud.

facts.statement: Although Nemegtomaia has been used to suggest that oviraptorosaurs were non-flying birds, the clade is generally considered a group of non-avian dinosaurs.
facts.quote: Aunque Nemegtomaia se ha utilizado para sugerir que los oviraptorosaurianos fueron pájaros no voladores, el clado generalmente se considera un grupo de dinosaurios no aviarios.

facts.statement: In 2010, researchers classified Nemegtomaia as a member of the Oviraptoridae family within the subfamily Ingeniinae.
facts.quote: En 2010, Longrich y sus colegas determinaron que Nemegtomaia pertenecía a la familia Oviraptoridae, como parte de la subfamilia Ingeniinae

facts.statement: In 2010, paleontologist Gregory S. Paul hypothesized that crested-less oviraptorids were juveniles or females of crested species.
facts.quote: En 2010, el paleontólogo estadounidense Gregory S. Paul sugirió que los oviraptóridos sin cresta eran juveniles o hembras de especies con crestas

facts.statement: In 2016, Gregory S. Paul listed Nemegtomaia as "Conchoraptor (=Nemegtomaia) barsboldi".
facts.quote: En 2016 lo enumeró como "Conchoraptor (=Nemegtomaia) barsboldi"

facts.statement: Researchers suggested that while crests are usually associated with Oviraptorinae, the trait might correlate with size and maturity in Ingeniinae.
facts.quote: Afirmaron que, aunque la presencia de crestas generalmente se asocia con Oviraptorinae en lugar de Ingeniinae, la característica puede estar correlacionada con el tamaño y la madurez

facts.statement: The subfamily name Ingeniinae was replaced by Heyuanninae because the name Ingenia was already occupied.
facts.quote: El nombre de la subfamilia Ingeniinae ha sido reemplazado por el nombre Heyuanninae, ya que Ingenia estaba ocupada

facts.statement: Nemegtomaia lived from the Campanian to the Maastrichtian stages, between 83.6 and 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Campanian to Maastrichtian (83.6 to 66 million years ago)

facts.statement: Nemegtomaia is distinguished by a unique combination of a crest, an enlarged first toe, and eight sacral vertebrae.
facts.quote: Aunque Nemegtomaia no posee ninguna característica única que lo distinga de otros oviraptóridos, autapomorfias, la combinación de una cresta, un primer dedo agrandado y una gran cantidad de vértebras sacras, ocho, es exclusiva de este taxón

facts.statement: Researchers concluded that most of the oviraptorid diet likely consisted of plant matter due to similarities with herbivores.
facts.quote: Longrich y sus colegas concluyeron que debido a las similitudes entre los oviraptóridos y los animales herbívoros, la mayor parte de su dieta probablemente se habría formado por materia vegetal

facts.statement: In 2017, Gregory F. Funston and colleagues suggested that parrot-like oviraptorid jaws may indicate a frugivorous diet including nuts and seeds.
